issues.claim: Compare untreated leachate with individually applied candidate treatments using split batches
issues.explanation: No candidate treatment or operating-condition range is identified, so the company and researcher cannot assess the actual bench comparison or its required process expertise. Briefly name the initial candidates and conditions, or explicitly require agreement of that screening matrix before the experiment starts.

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go: held-out effluent meets confirmed regulatory limits, including COD, accounting for uncertainty; containment predicts zero outward contaminant mass flux across the eastern boundary under agreed seasonal scenarios
issues.explanation: The effluent criterion does not define the acceptance unit, handling of repeated measurements or a statistical decision rule, while the flux criterion could pass on an inadequately validated model merely predicting zero. Make acceptance conditional on a pre-agreed batch/repeat aggregation and confidence rule, plus held-out model-validation tolerances and an uncertainty-based flux criterion for every agreed seasonal scenario.

issues.claim: Require uncertainty bounds supporting improvement; unresolved reference areas or insufficient pockets prevent a pass.
issues.explanation: This does not define a statistical pass condition for the detection improvement or the accompanying no-increase requirement on false positives, permitting acceptance based on favorable point estimates despite uncertainty consistent with worse performance. Add a brief prerequisite to pre-agree the confidence level and require the lower bound on the detection difference to exceed the agreed improvement threshold and the upper bound on the false-positive difference to satisfy the agreed tolerance, alongside the stated cost and turnaround caps.

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go: its upper 95% uncertainty bound is at most 10%, with lower error than municipality rating; insufficient independent claims means no pass.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be a method that takes our policy locations, matches them to hail intensity estimates at field level, and tells us which parts of our portfolio are priced too low.

issues.explanation: Aggregate mean claim severity can meet this rule through an overall pricing adjustment while assigning hail exposure incorrectly across fields or failing to identify underpriced segments; the qualitative field-matching prerequisites do not test that result. Retain the severity target but add a held-out acceptance rule for the calibration of segments selected on tuning data and a verifiable location-to-hazard matching criterion, with success conditional on agreeing both before evaluation.

issues.claim: Define severity error as absolute observed/assumed mean cost per confirmed hail claim minus one, with comparable coverage and developed losses.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

issues.explanation: The source establishes loss records, not a confirmed-hail evaluation set, and the proposal does not specify how repeated records become claims or how uncertain hail labels and unverifiable locations affect the evaluated denominator; selecting only readily confirmed, precisely located losses could yield a false portfolio-wide pass. Add a compact prerequisite to agree claim consolidation, independent hail confirmation, uncertain-label handling and evaluation coverage, restricting any acceptance claim to represented populations.

issues.claim: The company reports leachate COD of 3,400 mg/L. Zorić's zeolite-barrier study addresses ammonium-laden leachate, not demonstrated COD treatment.

sources.quote: our last sampling showed COD at 3,400 mg/L
Permeable reactive barriers (PRBs) using natural zeolite (clinoptilolite) represent an inexpensive passive remediation option for ammonium-laden leachate plumes in alluvial aquifers.

issues.explanation: Jev rates the support of this fact by its source sentences at 0.32. Keep in the fact only what the source states; move any condition, requirement or next step into proposedActions or questions.

issues.claim: the upper 95% uncertainty bound on outward contaminant mass flux across the eastern boundary is no greater than zero in every agreed seasonal scenario

sources.quote: We do not know how far the contamination has moved or which direction groundwater flows under the site at different seasons.
The liner under that area was never designed for liquid retention.

issues.explanation: An east-only flux gate could pass if groundwater or an intervention carries contamination toward another boundary, despite continuing uncontrolled migration. Require the containment gate to cover a locally justified control surface encompassing all plausible downgradient pathways under the agreed seasonal scenarios, rather than the eastern boundary alone.

issues.claim: Define severity error as absolute observed/assumed mean cost per confirmed hail claim minus one, using comparable coverage and developed losses. Proposed go/no-go: upper 95% uncertainty bound at most 10%, lower error than municipality rating, and the same 10% bound within each underpriced segment selected on tuning data.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be a method that takes our policy locations, matches them to hail intensity estimates at field level, and tells us which parts of our portfolio are priced too low.

Property claims for hail damage on Vojvodina farms are costing us about 18% more per claim than our pricing assumed; we believe we're underestimating exposure because we don't know how to map hail intensity at field level.

issues.explanation: The severity target directly addresses the reported per-claim excess, but it can pass even when hail frequency—and consequently portfolio underpricing—is substantially underestimated; including non-claimants in evaluation coverage does not make them enter this metric. Retain the severity target and add a held-out, segment-level observed-versus-priced loss-per-exposure acceptance rule, including non-claiming policies and an uncertainty bound, with its exposure denominator agreed before evaluation.

issues.claim: the upper 95% uncertainty bound on outward contaminant mass flux is no greater than zero across a locally justified control surface encompassing all plausible downgradient pathways in every agreed seasonal scenario.
issues.explanation: The first experiment describes field characterisation and bench screening but no implemented containment condition with field observations capable of supporting this gate; it also explicitly excludes model predictions alone as proof of containment. Separate the initial screening/design decision from a later containment-verification gate, making the latter conditional on an agreed field intervention, baseline and post-intervention flux evidence.

issues.claim: Require at least 95% correct asset-to-hazard-cell links against independently verified parcel boundaries and storm footprints, with matching protocols agreed beforehand.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

issues.explanation: Unlike the pricing-error targets, the matching target specifies neither its evaluated population and sampling rule nor a statistical acceptance condition; a small, easy-to-verify subset could achieve 95% observed correctness while portfolio-level field matching remains unreliable. Make acceptance conditional on a predeclared representative audit of evaluated policy-asset links, including non-claiming exposure, with a one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of at least 95% correctness and conservative treatment of unresolved links.

issues.claim: Her signature benchmarking experience suggests a strong methodological fit, but earlier Dilithium results cannot establish final ML-DSA correctness, memory fit or security on KL-HSM hardware.

sources.quote: Falcon-512 verification takes 2.11 ms but requires only 7.4 kB of stack, making it preferable for devices with less than 10 kB SRAM.
Signing is substantially more expensive for Falcon due to the discrete Gaussian sampler: 14.8 ms versus 3.2 ms for Dilithium-2.

issues.explanation: The fit rationale names the implementation work and its transfer limits but omits its reported trade-offs, particularly the distinction between verification memory and signing cost. Add one short sentence explaining that these published trade-offs motivate separate signing-latency and memory measurements, without treating the published numbers as KL-HSM forecasts.

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go requires all correctness and interoperability tests passing, measured resource use and performance within pre-agreed numerical limits, and no detected leakage under an agreed adequately powered screen. Insufficient evidence means unresolved, not pass.
issues.explanation: Numerical ceilings and an unspecified 'adequately powered' screen do not define when sampled p99 latency, throughput or a negative leakage result constitute sufficient evidence, allowing false acceptance from favourable samples or an insensitive screen. Require a frozen pre-evaluation acceptance specification defining workloads and repeats, confidence-bound rules for sampled performance, and the leakage screen's test threshold, sample size and sensitivity criterion; unresolved specifications must block go/no-go.

issues.claim: and p95/p99 latency increases at most 5% under company-approved representative load.

sources.quote: does not slow down search response times noticeably.

issues.explanation: Unlike the failure-rate and precision gates, the latency gate specifies only a threshold, not an uncertainty-aware acceptance rule; noisy tail-latency estimates could therefore pass despite a true slowdown above the agreed limit. Add a concise requirement that the 95% upper confidence bound on each p95/p99 relative increase be at most 5%, with insufficient precision leaving the decision unresolved.

issues.claim: Judge all evaluation queries, including nonzero results; evaluate overall and separate held-out cross-script, mixed-script and ambiguous-mapping populations.

sources.quote: When a user types a search term in Latin script and the stored document uses Cyrillic — or the other way around — our search returns no results even though the document is there.

issues.explanation: The combined cross-script population could meet every stated gate while the less frequent search direction still fails systematically, falsely accepting a solution that does not address the company's bidirectional problem. Add Latin-query/Cyrillic-document and Cyrillic-query/Latin-document populations to the existing separate held-out acceptance gates, retaining an unresolved decision when either lacks sufficient evidence.

sources.quote: When a user types a search term in Latin script and the stored document uses Cyrillic — or the other way around — our search returns no results even though the document is there.

issues.explanation: Returning irrelevant hits for previously zero-hit searches eliminates the counted failure while preserving their baseline P@10 of zero, so the proposal could accept without making the existing relevant contracts findable.
